subject.title: Apply design-system composer to app chat UI

question: Should the native composer redesign and the new persisted Chat Settings surface land together, including both the restored inline speaker-mute control and the Settings speech toggle?
rationale: The branch changes the primary chat interaction model and adds persisted configuration; tests cannot determine whether the combined control placement and duplicated speech surface match the intended product direction.

options.title: Split composer and settings
options.body: Land the composer and flyout redesign separately, preserve current control placement and defaults, and review persisted Settings relocation as a focused follow-up.

options.title: Sponsor the combined UX
options.body: Keep the combined branch, explicitly approve both speech-control surfaces and the new tool-call setting, then require translations and current-head UI proof.

options.title: Defer the redesign
options.body: Pause this PR until the broader design-system direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/962 is accepted or replaced by a maintainer-owned design.

recommendation.title: Split composer and settings
recommendation.body: Land the composer and flyout redesign separately, preserve current control placement and defaults, and review persisted Settings relocation as a focused follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest recent merged-history signal for native chat UX and composer-adjacent behavior.
